extensions.scope: Teacher dashboard — Day Clock · stripped, Panel skin, Libre Franklin. Other wireframe options and the Ledger skin are outside this system.
extensions.derivation: Six colour literals exist: primary, info, success, error, focus, neutral. Every other colour is written hsl(from var(--core) h s <lightness>%). Both neutral ramps are cut from the neutral seed; state colours keep core hue and core saturation and move lightness only.

primary.note: Java Beach, from colorspec.pdf. At full brightness only on marks carrying no text: calendar dots, caret.

primary-ink.note: The step primary takes when it carries text. 32% is the ceiling: white is 4.53:1 here, 4.29:1 at 33%.

info.note: SCHEDULED. Renders at 64% lightness on dark, 38% on light; chroma .121/.122.

success.note: FINISHED. Renders at 65% lightness on dark, 34% on light; chroma .125/.123.

error.note: The now-rule across the hour rail. error-deep (38%) carries its white clock label.

focus.note: Bleu de France. Focus ring only; never a surface.

neutral.note: The seed both mode ramps are cut from. Saturation drops with lightness so pale steps do not go blue.

modeRamps.parity: Measured across eight text-on-ground pairs; total light/dark contrast drift is 7.76. State pairs are matched on OKLCH chroma rather than contrast ratio.

brand.purpose: The FRANKLYN wordmark in the bar. Tight tracking by rule.

pin.purpose: The exam PIN. The only monospaced element in the system.

head.purpose: The two filled primary heads: TODAY and LAST EXAM.

body.purpose: Controls, button label, user chip, rail block titles.

label.purpose: Day gutter, scroll sentinels, side-block headings.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Separates a surface from its ground. Never grows for emphasis.

extensions.motionNote: No motion tokens. The system has no transitions or animations; state changes are instantaneous fill swaps. Any motion added later must be authored as one orchestrated moment, not scattered hovers.
extensions.breakpointNote: None. One fluid grid capped at 1300px with a fixed 300px side column; nothing is dropped or reflowed at any width. Desktop only, per PRODUCT.md.

components.name: Exam Card
components.description: Four slots: PIN, title and time, state. The PIN leads because it is what gets spoken aloud.
components.css: .ds-card-exam { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 20px; background: hsl(222 14% 18%); border: 0; border-radius: 6px; padding: 16px 24px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px hsl(222 40% 4% / .24); cursor: pointer; } .ds-card-exam:hover { background: hsl(222 12% 24%); } .ds-card-exam__pin { font: 500 24px/1.1 "Chivo Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; color: hsl(222 0% 97%); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-card-exam__title { display: block; font: 500 18px/1.35 "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; color: hsl(222 0% 97%); } .ds-card-exam__time { display: block; margin-top: 1px; font: 400 13px/1.35 "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; color: hsl(222 11% 69%); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-card-exam__state { font: 700 13px "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .06em; color: hsl(200 85% 64%); }

components.name: Exam Card — Finished
components.description: A finished exam drains. The card itself is drawn identically; only the PIN and state change colour.
components.css: .ds-card-done { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 20px; background: hsl(222 14% 18%); border: 0; border-radius: 6px; padding: 16px 24px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px hsl(222 40% 4% / .24); cursor: pointer; } .ds-card-done:hover { background: hsl(222 12% 24%); } .ds-card-done__pin { font: 500 24px/1.1 "Chivo Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; color: hsl(222 11% 69%); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-card-done__title { display: block; font: 500 18px/1.35 "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; color: hsl(222 0% 97%); } .ds-card-done__time { display: block; margin-top: 1px; font: 400 13px/1.35 "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; color: hsl(222 11% 69%); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-card-done__state { font: 700 13px "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .06em; color: hsl(145 55% 65%); }

components.name: Region Head
components.description: The system's only highlight device: a filled block of primary-ink carrying white. Used exactly twice — TODAY and LAST EXAM.
components.css: .ds-region-head { background: hsl(185 72% 32%); color: #fff; padding: 12px 20px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0; } .ds-region-head b { font: 700 14px/1.3 "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .09em; color: #fff; }

components.name: Brand Bar
components.description: Full-bleed primary-ink strip. Firefly is deliberately not used here — it vanishes against the navy ground.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; background: hsl(185 72% 32%); padding: 16px 20px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px hsl(222 40% 4% / .24); } .ds-nav__brand { font: 800 22px "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .04em; color: #fff; } .ds-nav__user { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font: 600 14px "Libre Franklin", sans-serif; color: #fff; cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav__avatar { width: 26px; height: 26px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; }

components.name: Now Rule
components.description: The current minute across the hour rail. Rides over the page and restyles nothing beneath it.
components.css: .ds-now { position: relative; height: 2px; background: hsl(0 78% 55%); margin: 28px 0; } .ds-now b { position: absolute; left: 0; top: -9px; padding: 1px 5px; background: hsl(0 78% 38%); color: #fff; border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0; font: 500 11px "Chivo Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; }

narrative.overview:
This is the surface a teacher glances at while standing in front of a room of people. They are not reading it; they are checking it between laps, from a few feet away, with a PIN they have just read out loud still in their head. Everything here follows from that: the ground is dark and quiet so nothing competes, the typography is sized for a glance rather than a session, and the two things that matter right now — what is running today, and what happened last — are the only loud objects on the page.

The system has no decorative lines. Stylistically there are none at all: every boundary is a step in fill, and anything that needs emphasis becomes a filled block rather than a bordered one. This is the single mechanic the whole surface runs on, and it is what keeps a dense screen from reading as a grid of cells. A line is drawn only when it does work no fill can do and beats the fill outright — a measured scale, a marked minute — never to style, enclose or separate. Colour is rationed hard — the ground, the text ramp and the structure are neutral, and the only saturated things on screen are the brand bar, the one primary action, the two region heads, the exam-state labels, and the red rule marking the current minute.

The anti-reference is explicit and was named by the owner: the generic AI-SaaS dashboard — hairline borders on every container, pill-shaped badges, soft radii, one blue accent scattered everywhere. Also rejected: anything that reads as "elegant". This is an educational platform for a technical secondary school, not a luxury brand, and undersized type with wide tracking was identified as the tell.
keyCharacteristics: Borderless: separation is tonal, never ruled; a line only where it is the functional mark, as on the hour scale
Dark-grounded on a desaturated navy, with a light mode of equal semantic weight
Colour only where it carries meaning; neutral everywhere else
One monospaced element on the whole page, and it is the PIN
Emphasis is always a filled block, never an added edge
Full-viewport; the page never scrolls, only the timeline does

rules.name: The Core-Only Rule
rules.body: Six colour literals exist: primary, info, success, error, focus, neutral. Every other colour in the system is written hsl(from var(--core) h s <lightness>%). A new colour that cannot be expressed as a lightness step off one of the six does not belong in the system.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Full-brightness primary never carries text. The moment a teal surface needs a label on it, it drops to primary-ink. There is no third option.

rules.name: The Chroma Parity Rule
rules.body: The light and dark state colours are matched on OKLCH chroma (.122/.121 blue, .123/.125 green), not on contrast ratio. Matching ratios produces a dark navy label on white that reads as ink rather than signal. Both state pairs keep their core hue and core saturation; only lightness moves per mode.

rules.name: The Spoken Number Rule
rules.body: The PIN is the only monospaced element on the page. It is a code a teacher reads out loud to a room and a student types into a terminal; the fixed advance is what makes the digits scannable. Monospace anywhere else is a costume.

rules.name: The Dashboard Density Rule
rules.body: The styleguide's 16px body-text floor is written for document copy. UI labels sit below it on purpose — scaling the whole page to 16px reads as a browser zoomed to 120%. Only the state label was ever genuinely undersized for the room it occupies.

rules.name: The Whisper Rule
rules.body: A detail that becomes prominent stops being a detail. The shadow is 1px with a 2px blur and never grows — not on hover, not on focus, not for emphasis. Elevation is communicated by fill.

rules.name: The No-Line Rule
rules.body: Every boundary on this surface is a step in fill. If two regions need separating, one of them changes tone, and a border added to solve a separation problem is the wrong fix. The rule yields only to a higher bar: when a line is so clearly the better drawing that its being out of place still reads better than any fill, take the line. "A fill would also work here" is not that bar. Measured scales are where this keeps happening — an hour grid divides on lines because divisions are what a scale is made of, where tonal banding turns a continuous axis into stacked blocks.

rules.name: The Filled Block Rule
rules.body: A highlight is a filled block of primary, never an extra line added to something that already has edges. The system uses this device exactly twice — the TODAY region head and the LAST EXAM head — and a third would dilute both.

dos: Do derive every new colour from one of the six core values by overriding lightness: hsl(from var(--fr-primary) h s 40%).
Do separate regions by stepping tone: bg → surface → raise.
Do drop primary to primary-ink the moment a teal surface carries text.
Do match light and dark on chroma when a colour's job is to signal, not on contrast ratio.
Do keep the 4px spacing scale (8/12/16/24/32) for anything that is rhythm.
Do use Bootstrap Icons, per the styleguide, sized off the adjacent label's cap height.
Do let geometry locked to the 150px spine gutter stay literal, and comment why.
donts: Don't add a border to any container. Not a hairline, not a keyline, not a coloured left edge. Drawing a line because it is genuinely the better mark is not covered by this; adding one to separate things is.
Don't add a second highlight device. A filled block of primary is the only one, and it is already spent on TODAY and LAST EXAM.
Don't let the now-layer restyle what sits under it.
Don't use monospace for anything but the PIN.
Don't put full-brightness primary under text — it is 2.41:1 against white.
Don't scale UI labels up to the styleguide's 16px document floor; the page reads as browser-zoomed.
Don't grow the shadow for emphasis. It is 1px and stays 1px.
Don't reach for pill radii, soft 8–12px corners, or status badges in chip form.
